A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Loopy, and their main text, equations, tables and figures support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, although v3 refers to appendix details for training data and motion metrics, including an unresolved 'Appendix ??' reference. Those details cannot be assessed.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component and sampling ablations in Tables 1–3, and a ten-user subjective evaluation in Figure 5.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds HDTF evaluations, training-data controls, additional motion metrics and objective openset comparisons.

M1.justification: The reported conditioning inputs narrow: Sections 3.1 and 3.3 of v1 explicitly include a separate landmark-sequence condition, whereas v3 lists audio, head-movement variance and expression variance. The dual temporal modules, audio-to-latents mechanism, diffusion loss and audio-only inference remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds HDTF evaluation in Table 3; v1 names HDTF only as training data. CelebV-HQ, RAVDESS and the same categories of openset images and audio remain. This extends evaluation within portrait generation rather than introducing a new task. Broader training-source changes cannot be established from the supplied descriptions.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add Hallo*, retrained on the authors' dataset. Table 3 additionally includes SadTalker, EchoMimic, Hallo, Hallo* and VExpress in the objective openset comparison, where v1 reported only Loopy variants. These extend comparisons using existing method families; the original benchmark and user-study comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends the evaluation design with training-data controls: Hallo trained on the authors' data and Loopy trained without collected data. It introduces DGlo and DExp as ground-truth motion-deviation metrics. Tables 1–2 stop reporting smoothness, although openset evaluation retains it. These are additions to the protocols, not evidence that the unchanged benchmark results were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing component-removal, temporal-range and sampling ablations are retained and extended to HDTF in Table 3. A Loopy(HDTF) variant, described as trained without collected data, adds an analysis of training-data contribution. The original ablation questions and openset evidence otherwise remain.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both describe ten user-study participants. Motion variance is a model input or evaluation quantity, not uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial results for Hallo*, DGlo/DExp, objective openset comparisons and HDTF comparisons/ablations. For example, HDTF FVD-R is 10.443 for full Loopy and 12.742 for Loopy(HDTF). Shared scores in Tables 1–2, original openset ablation scores and Figure 5 voting results are unchanged. Smoothness scores and ground-truth rows disappear from Tables 1–2; these changes do not demonstrate same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 2 changes from selecting a segment midpoint to indexing distinct uniformly spaced frames using the within-segment offset i mod s. This corrects the mathematical specification to match the uniform-sampling description already present in v1. The diffusion objective remains unchanged, and neither version adds theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an audio-driven portrait diffusion model that avoids inference-time spatial motion constraints, uses long-term temporal information and audio-to-latents conditioning, and improves naturalness, stability and synthesis quality. v3 emphasizes subtle facial expressions more clearly without materially redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation that classifier-free guidance can stabilize videos by copying reference poses and interprets Hallo* results as evidence for architectural benefits. It replaces the small-stride FPS-mismatch explanation with insufficient motion information and appearance reliance. It also omits v1's explicit warning about long-sequence color shifts and artifacts.

D1.justification: v3 specifies 128 learned tokens, 256 attention channels, a 1280-channel projection, five temporal segments, four days per training stage and masking of ungenerated motion frames. It reports 174 training hours, versus v1's 160 collected hours plus unspecified public-data supplementation; this does not establish a 14-hour increase. Referenced appendix details are unavailable, and the project URL is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds MobilePortrait, CyberHost, Real3D-Portrait and Chung and Zisserman's lip-sync work. Related work briefly expands to NeRF rendering and gives DiffusedHeads more explicit positioning. The underlying GAN-versus-diffusion organization and Loopy's positioning against spatially constrained methods remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanations and experimental discussion undergo extensive rewriting, including retained material. v3 reorganizes the motivation, adds internal method subheadings and expands the explanation of attention and baseline evaluation. The overall section order remains, while the header changes from preprint to ICLR 2025 publication.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 are redrawn with clearer module grouping, symbols and tensor dimensions. Tables 1–2 change their row and column structure, and Table 3 becomes a grouped openset/HDTF comparison and ablation table. Qualitative panels in Figures 1 and 6 are rearranged or replaced. Figure 5 retains identical chart content.

improvement.justification: The added training-data controls and HDTF evaluations strengthen the empirical support, while the corrected sampling equation and explicit audio-to-latents dimensions improve reproducibility. These gains are tempered by unavailable appendix details, incomplete specification of the new motion-error metrics, and removal of smoothness and ground-truth entries from Tables 1–2. Overall, v3 provides a clearer and better-supported paper without resolving all documentation gaps.
